blocks.orig: Kigoma is a town and lake port in northwestern Tanzania, on the northeastern shores of Lake Tanganyika. It is close to the border with Burundi and The Democratic Republic of the Congo. The city serves as the capital for the surrounding Kigoma Region and is hub for everyone who wants to trek Chimpanzees in Gombe Stream and Mahale Mountains national park.
blocks.html: In the northwest of Tanzania, on the northeastern shore of Lake Tanganyika, lies the town and lake port of Kigoma. The borders with Burundi and The Democratic Republic of the Congo are nearby. Kigoma is the capital of the Kigoma Region that surrounds it, and it is the base for anyone planning to trek chimpanzees in Gombe Stream or Mahale Mountains national park.

blocks.orig: Kigoma is easy to reach by plane from Dar Es Salaam and Arusha/Moshi. In Kigoma you find the Livingstone Memorial Museum. The famous site where Stanley uttered the immortal words, ‘Dr Livingstone, I presume?’ on meeting Livingstone in 1871. The two mango trees here are said to have been grafted from the original tree that shaded the two men during their encounter. The Livingstone Memorial Museum holds some artefacts and printed placards about the East African slave trade. And you find paintings by local artists and papier-mâché replicas of Stanley and Livingstone. Livingstone and Stanley’s story is worth knowing! And the humble museum’s effort to recount the horrors of the slave trade makes it an interesting stop.
blocks.html: Flights from Dar Es Salaam and from Arusha/Moshi make Kigoma simple to reach. The town is home to the Livingstone Memorial Museum. This is the well-known spot where Stanley greeted Livingstone in 1871 with the immortal line, ‘Dr Livingstone, I presume?’ The two mango trees growing here are said to be grafts from the original tree that shaded the two men during that meeting. Inside, the Livingstone Memorial Museum displays a number of artefacts and printed placards on the East African slave trade, alongside paintings by local artists and papier-mâché figures of Stanley and Livingstone. The story of Livingstone and Stanley is one worth knowing, and the modest museum’s attempt to tell the horrors of the slave trade makes it a worthwhile stop.

blocks.orig: Kigoma is located on beautiful Lake Tanganyika. It is not only a city with a long history and exciting culture, but also the ideal starting point for a chimpanzee trekking in Gombe Stream or Mahale Mountains National Park.
blocks.html: Set on the shores of beautiful Lake Tanganyika, Kigoma is more than a town with a long history and a lively culture: it is also the perfect base from which to begin a chimpanzee trek in Gombe Stream or Mahale Mountains National Park.
